warning_texts: This profile is single-vendor: the architect, every worker, every auditor and this red team are all Claude Opus, so a mistake the model is prone to can appear on both sides of every check, and no cross-vendor or GPT gate exists anywhere in this system.
The only layers that really hold are the deterministic ones: the machine gates, the frozen check_plan, the control lock and the release surface gate.

Write protection over raw_data/, audit/tools/ and .claude/ was permissions.deny on the edit tools, not on the shell, so a changed raw file would have been caught by the control lock after the fact rather than prevented.
My raw recomputation agrees with every figure the machine gates derived from raw, but the lock hashes are not among my inputs, so I did not verify byte-level integrity of the raw export.

No deterministic rule reads release prose that contains no number, and nothing compares a published surface with its generator's output: the release surface gate (21 of 21 bound), gate_release_document (claims and caveats rendered) and gate_release_auditor all passed a report whose R03 sentence is f

Every LLM step result in this run carries no substantive evidence, only 'driver e2e' summaries and one-line notes files; this covers gate0_semantic, the four gate_*_auditor steps and the four worker_* steps.

Those step results also repeat an identical 'recomputed 0.473684' check even on stages that never compute the refund rate, such as worker_clean, and all carry the placeholder timestamp 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z.
Taken together, the chain of intermediate PASS verdicts adds no independent judgment beyond the machine gates and this red team.
The spec period ends on 2025-03-30, yet metrics name it 2025-Q1-delivered and questions.md calls it the reported quarter, which ends on 2025-03-31.

No row in this export is dated 2025-03-31, so no published number moves, but on a later export March 31 would silently drop out of net revenue 35741.52, the country split and the refund rate 0.473684.

The assumption behind the refund rate that looks weakest is what counts as a refunded customer: any refund above zero counts, including partial ones such as 13.08 of 26.15, and the spec does not pin this down.

That reading gives the published 0.473684 (27 of 57 customers). Counting only fully refunded customers gives 0.210526 (12 of 57), and the order-row basis the spec rejected gives 0.189655 (33 of 174), which is 2.50 times lower.

The ruling revenue_recognition = net_of_refunds nets each refund against its order's date because the export has no refund date, so net revenue 35741.52 (refunds 4493.50) includes refunds that may have been issued after 2025-03-30, which the data cannot confirm.
Net revenue is invoiced gross minus refunds on delivered orders, not cash collected.

The spec declares every amount as EUR, including PL and CZ rows, but the export has no currency column, so the single-currency assumption behind 35741.52 and the three country figures cannot be verified from the data.

timezone_for_dates = Europe/Warsaw is applied trivially because order_date is a plain date with no time, and no release surface tells the reader that dates are Warsaw-local; no number moves on this export.
R05 (customer lifetime value) is excused only inside audit/check_plan.json, and no release surface tells the reader that R05 was not answered or why.
R04's row accounting (201 raw rows, 174 kept, 26 not delivered, 1 outside the period) exists only in analysis/answers/R04.json and appears on no release surface.
All four worker carries are copies of one template whose population definition says only status=delivered, leaving the period filter to a separate periods field.
None of the four carries records the pitfall that gross is not net, which is the pitfall the published report broke.
All four carries list raw_data/orders.csv under do_not_reread although it is a raw source rather than a previous stage's output.

gate_metrics_machine does not recompute excluded_outside_period or excluded_order_rows directly (see its unchecked.json); they are pinned only by component sums, and my raw recount confirms 1 row (O00201, dated 2025-04-01, 999.99 EUR) and 27 rows.

check_plan.json accepts gate_release_document's claims_rendered and caveats_rendered as unproven because the plan proof could not find the claim register in its temporary copy, so neither rule was ever shown to fire on a broken release.
The handoff has no drift_since_review field; that absence does not show that assumptions reviewed on another export still hold.

I could not establish four things from my inputs: when refunds were issued, which currency PL and CZ rows are in, whether the carry files pass audit/schemas/carry.schema.json (outside my allowed inputs), and whether raw bytes match the Gate 0 lock.
summary: FAIL on one release defect, raised as two blockers. All 21 rendered numbers on the three surfaces match, and the country figures reconcile to the headline. Where the report fails is its prose.
